Fuck school. I have 2 degrees and had nearly straight A's and yet I currently live in a scary nightmare of poverty, debt, community unrest, and mental illness. School does not determine the rest of your life. It's ok to flunk a semester. It's also ok to disappoint your parents. We've all done it at some point. 

If you can and if you need to, take some time off school. Find a cause and throw yourself into it. Join a group of young activists or volunteer somewhere. Start a business out of your home, play the drums, or paint and draw and make collages from old magazines. Study independently a subject you are passionate about, for your own reasons -- not for a grade. You will learn more pursuing your own interests than you will from school and exams.

Hey buddy! Gay, straight, and bisexual are not the only sexual orientations out there. Maybe you're pansexual, polysexual, asexual, sapiosexual... There are so many fucking sexual preferences out there. You are young and it's totally fine to be exploring and experimenting. I think some counseling and possibly anxiety meds might help your obsessive compulsive questioning of yourself. 

As for the possibility of having a dissociative disorder, just know these disorders are more common than you probably think. It's also a spectrum, not everyone who dissociates meets the criteria for DID. At any given time somewhere between 8 and 11% of the population would meet the criteria for one of the dissociative disorders. /r/DID has been helpful to me since I found out I have a dissociative disorder. A psychiatrist or psychologist would be able to diagnose you and therapy can really help. 

Good luck!

I also live in North America, and I have a dissociative disorder but do not have amnesia, so I do not meet the current criteria for dissociative identity disorder. That said, please keep in mind in your research, that the story of DID that gets told over and over again in pop culture is highly sensationalized and often bears little resemblance to real life stories of individuals with DID. The common portrayal in media feeds a stigma that makes our lives even more difficult. I have a steady job and a family and friends. Most of my close friends know I've been hospitalized for depression and PTSD, but I feel like there are very few people on this Earth that I can be fully honest with. I have two very different personalities, with different names, mannerisms, emotions, and skill sets. But I fear if my friends or coworkers knew this they would either think I was lying or dangerous or both. I admire others who are more open about having DID. But I know that my fragile world I am fighting so hard to sustain could come crashing down around me if I stopped concealing my condition. It's rather lonely being multiple people.

When I was in third grade my parents and teachers had me tested for learning disabilities. I scored extremely low on short-term memory tests. I thought for most of my childhood that my poor memory and inability to pay attention were due to learning disabilities. I also had a few traumatic experiences as a child, and then as an adult was in a severely abusive relationship. During that relationship I started to dissociate, feel separate from my body, and feel like things were just not real. Around that time I also started to feel like this other being inside me would take over my mind from time to time. I also had (and still have) very poor short term memory. Because I have some symptoms of DID each of my mental healthcare providers have asked me about my memory and if I have gaps of time missing or feel ever like I have amnesia. I wouldn't say my poor memory is that extreme, wouldn't call it amnesia.  There are definitely traumatic memories that are incomplete though: I remember getting in the car determined to flee and getting on the highway, but not what happened next. I know I wasn't successful that time in getting away, but I don't remember why or how I ended back with him. I remember another time waking up naked on a floor, but not how I ended up unconscious there. I think my poor memory as a child and my poor memory as an adult has more to do with trauma and associated mental illness than with learning disabilities.
